title: A pattern does not prove a cause
summary: Two things can change together without one causing the other. A third factor or the way data was collected may explain the pattern.
introduction: Two things can change together without one causing the other. A third factor or the way data was collected may explain the pattern. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain a pattern does not prove a cause
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Two things can change together without one causing the other. A third factor or the way data was collected may explain the pattern.

blocks.code:
Observed: more ice cream sales and more swimming on hot days
Possible shared cause: warm weather
Unsupported claim: buying ice cream makes people swim
blocks.title: A pattern does not prove a cause

blocks.text: The observation shows a pattern. It does not tell us that one activity caused the other. We need a suitable study to support a cause claim.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name a factor that could affect both umbrella sales and wet roads.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not turn a shared pattern into a cause claim without evidence.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).

seo.title: Data Science: A pattern does not prove a cause
